name: 01_intro
label: GeoResponse — a decision you can defend
text: GeoResponse turns satellite imagery into a decision a manager can defend. Not a map demo: a decision, the evidence behind it, and a human correction. In this video we use a real example case in the Ahr valley, with real Sentinel-2 images.

name: 02_sources
label: Demo pack vs my workspace
text: There are two data sources. The demo pack is the bundled synthetic scenario for a stage or booth. My workspace is your own sites. You switch in Settings, and the demo pack stays one click away.

name: 03_empty
label: An empty workspace
text: The workspace starts empty. Import a CSV or GeoJSON, add one site manually, or load the bundled example. This is the difference between a demo and a product you can put your own data into.

name: 04_load
label: Load the example case
text: We load the example case: six sites in the Ahr supply corridor. Each row carries coordinates, severity, confidence, value, population, access and notes.

name: 05_map
label: Map, rows and summary
text: Every site becomes a pin and a row. Red is high risk, orange is watch. The summary gives the decision-maker the shape of the problem: six sites, how many red, value at risk, and people.

name: 06_edit
label: It is your data
text: This is not a fixed demo. Select a site and edit its name, coordinates, severity, confidence, value, population or access. Changes are saved in this browser until you connect a backend.

name: 07_export
label: Export CSV or GeoJSON
text: Export the list as CSV or GeoJSON. The point is not to trap your data in this app; it is to move the decision into the tools your team already uses.

name: 08_watch
label: The proactive inbox
text: The site list is one half. The other half is Watch, the proactive inbox. For this example we used the API: twelve quiet baseline values, then observations over time. The last observation crossed the threshold and produced this alert.

name: 09_evidence
label: Evidence, SLA and why
text: Watch shows the alert, not just a pin: severity, confidence, the SLA clock, the owner, the real Sentinel before and after, the value at risk, access, and why it fired against the baseline. The human sees the evidence before acting.

name: 10_agent
label: Ask the agent
text: Now ask the agent. It answers from grounded tools: the portfolio briefing, this alert, and coverage. It does not guess from a prompt: it calls get_briefing, get_alert and get_coverage, and you can see each step. The answer is slower than a chat box because the work is real: it reads the alert, the baseline, the SLA and the evidence, then proposes one safe next action. Notice the answer names the alert, the baseline, the SLA and the evidence; it does not invent a number. Every write is a proposal. Nothing is approved automatically. The system never approves a claim, dispatches a crew or signs an assessment. That is the difference between an assistant and an autonomous system.

name: 11_approve
label: A human approves
text: The agent proposes assigning a team. A human approves it here. The alert changes, the action is audited, and the proposal can be undone. The system never signs, dispatches or approves a claim on its own.

name: 12_demo
label: The demo pack is still there
text: Switch back to the demo pack whenever you need the synthetic scenarios for a stage. Your workspace is untouched. Both paths exist on purpose: one to show, one to use.

name: 13_close
label: Your sites, your decision
text: Real imagery. A ranked decision. A human correction. A proactive watch. That is GeoResponse: your sites, your evidence, your decision.
